For a fixed compressor power, the cooling provided by the refrigerant (Q ) decreases as the ambient temperature increases. This causes the dip in evaporator Q near 3pm. This drop is more pronounced in Los Angeles because the ambient evaporator temperature is higher than in Baltimore. The TES makes up the difference (Q ) between the TES,net cooling provided by the refrigerant and that being delivered to the cooling coil. The peak power from noon-6pm and the electric energy use over the 24 h period are summarized in Table 4. Compared to the serpentine design, using microchannels reduces the peak power by a further 17% in Los Angeles and 19% in Baltimore. It also reduces total energy use over the day. Alternatively, the peak-power reduction can be kept the same as the serpentine design using microchannels, but with a much smaller battery: ~4 tonh, and also with a smaller energy penalty. Changing the transition temperature of the PCM to 10 °C can still provide the same peak-load reduction as the 4.5 C, but with lower 24 h energy use. In fact, the energy use for the baseline variable-speed RTU and the hybrid TES are nearly the same when using a PCM with a transition temperature near 10 °C. 24 This report is available at no cost from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) at www.nrel.gov/publications. The differences in energy use are driven by the evaporator and condenser temperatures, and the evaporator temperature is the primary difference between the three TES heat exchanger designs. Table 5 shows these evaporator temperatures for the cases in Los Angeles. There are three key points to take away from this table. First, the evaporator temperature depends on the TES SOC of, with high SOC (>90% just before noon) requiring the lowest evaporator temperature, and low SOC (~10%) allowing for much higher evaporator temperatures. This is also shown in Figure 15, which shows the evaporator and glycol temperatures from 0% to 100% state of charge. Second, the evaporator temperature increases when using the microchannel design because it brings the glycol and refrigerant next to each other, rather than being separated by the composite PCM. Finally, increasing the PCM transition temperature (10 °C from 4.5 °C) increases the evaporator temperature up by a similar amount (~5.5 °C) when the SOC is in the middle range (PCM is changing phase), but has a smaller impact at the ends (<10% and >90% SOC).
